audit.why: Both layers already read Fiora / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill, matching the packet levelChart exactly and matching the mirror audit, which records setting win[0], win[1], win[3], win[5] and win[6] to these values deliberately. The packet flags 'chart contradicts data: Fiora wins 52.96% but the chart gives Cassiopeia 4/7 stages' — but the prose explains that cleanly: the win rate lives in the post-lane flank and side-lane window, not in the lane phase. I did not touch the chart. Changing it would fight the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names no cooldowns, and phases[5].why still says 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes' on a row both layers give to Cassiopeia. Left alone this time only because the row's rating and side are already correct and the length band is tight; the higher-value fixes were elsewhere.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — the same 24s at rank 1 as your Riposte, which makes 'bait it, then commit' a real timer rather than a slogan. Petrifying Gaze is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Miasma's 24s written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tells the player five separate times to 'parry his Miasma' and report[5].t ends in the meaningless token 'Riposte his KA'. Miasma is a persistent ground cloud, not an immobilizing cast — parrying it is not a thing you can do, and even standing in it the grounding is not what upgrades Riposte's return to a stun.
audit.why: Riot's Riposte text stuns only if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect. In this kit the one immobilize is Petrifying Gaze — a frontal stun on 120s at rank 1 — which is exactly what the content layer already tells the player to hold W for. The full layer was pointing the same cooldown at the wrong ability. Separately, Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia off poisoned targets on a 0.75s cooldown, which is the actual case for early Grievous Wounds and appears nowhere in the itemization line.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, report[0].t, report[1].t, tradeBad, dosFull[2].t and report[5].t now point Riposte at Petrifying Gaze and state the immobilize condition; Miasma is described as a grounding field to bait rather than parry; dontsFull[2].d and report[8].t now carry the Twin Fang heal and the anti-heal buy.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cassiopeia is called 'he'/'his' in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, breakdown.trading, report[0], report[1], report[2], report[3], report[4], report[5] and report[12] — sixteen strings on a champion the content layer correctly calls 'she' throughout.
audit.why: The two layers of the same page disagree on the enemy's gender, which is the most visible possible sign that the full layer was never written for this matchup.

notes: The content layer here is already strong and mirror-corrected; I left it entirely alone and spent every edit on the full layer, which was template boilerplate calling Cassiopeia 'he' sixteen times and telling the player five times to parry Miasma — a persistent ground cloud that cannot be parried. All of those now point Riposte at Petrifying Gaze, which is the one immobilize in her kit and therefore the only cast that upgrades the return to a stun. I did not touch the level chart: it matches the packet and the mirror exactly, and although the packet flags it as contradicting the 52.96% win rate, the content layer's 'late' text explains where that win rate comes from (the post-lane flank), so the chart is deliberate rather than broken. Carried forward the mirror's caution about the 'percent-max-HP true damage' description of Vitals — Riot's Duelist's Dance text mentions no damage type at all, and the trueDamage flag sits on Grand Challenge, not the passive. I neither repeated nor deleted that claim.
